blocks.title: Risk assessment and management
blocks.text: Risk assessment and management means identifying potential risks that could affect a project's success, analysing their likelihood and impact, and developing strategies to manage them. Effective risk management keeps projects on track, within budget and up to quality standards.

items: Identify risks: list everything that could affect the project, such as technical risks (technology changes), operational risks (resource shortages) or external risks (market fluctuations).
Analyse risks: judge each risk's likelihood and impact to decide which need most attention.
Develop mitigation strategies: plan how to reduce each significant risk's likelihood or impact, for example schedule buffers, backup resources or extra testing.
Monitor and review: keep watching for new risks and adjust the strategies as needed.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.text: A project uses a new, untested technology, and the risk is that it may not work as expected, causing delays and extra cost. Mitigation: run a small pilot project to test the technology before fully integrating it, so problems surface early without harming the main project.
